title: 6 Best Compact Tractors in 2026: Weight, Hitch and Dealer
keywords: best compact tractor for the money
description: The Kubota BX23S is the best compact tractor for 2 to 5 acres thanks to its loader and backhoe package; Kubota L2502 leads for 5 to 20 acres of ground work.
dek: The Kubota BX23S is the best compact tractor for 2 to 5 acres thanks to its loader and backhoe package; Kubota L2502 leads for 5 to 20 acres of ground work.
intro: The best compact tractor for most two-to-five-acre properties is the Kubota BX23S, because it ships as a tractor, loader and quick-detach backhoe package with four-wheel drive standard. If your land runs five to twenty acres with pasture, gravel and real ground work, the full-compact Kubota L2502 is the better machine.

Horsepower and the paint color get most of the attention, but on a small property four other things decide whether you are happy: operating weight, the three-point hitch category, loader lift capacity and how far you live from a dealer who can fix the tractor in July. This guide ranks six tractors in the 25-horsepower neighborhood on those points, then answers the sizing, transmission, implement and safety questions buyers ask most.
quickAnswer: Buy the Kubota BX23S if digging is on your list, the John Deere 1025R if weekly mowing and dealer support come first, and the Kioti CS2520 if you want the most warranty and equipment per dollar. Step up to the Kubota L2502 for five to twenty acres of heavier work. Budget buyers with a nearby LS dealer should look at the LS MT225S.

sections.h: The 6 Best Compact Tractors in 2026 at a Glance

blocks.p: On two to five acres, a sub-compact covers mowing, loader chores and snow, and the **Kubota BX23S** leads because the backhoe is part of the package and comes off without tools. With five to twenty acres of pasture, driveway and woodland work, buy a full compact such as the **Kubota L2502**. Everyone else picks from the table by job and dealer.

blocks.p: Every machine on this list sits in the low-to-mid 20s of engine horsepower, the class most people mean when they search for the best 25 hp tractor. The differences that matter are in frame weight, hitch category, loader package and the dealer behind the machine. Confirm current specs, warranty and package pricing with a local dealer before you sign, because brands revise these every model year.

sections.h: The 6 Best Compact Tractors in 2026, Ranked

blocks.p: The ranking weighs manufacturer specifications (engine type, transmission, hitch category, loader package and warranty), dealer coverage and the themes that come up again and again in owner forums. These machines were not run in field trials for this guide, so the text says when a point comes from a spec sheet and when it comes from owner reports.

blocks.h3: Best Overall: Kubota BX23S

blocks.p: The BX23S is sold as a complete tractor-loader-backhoe (TLB) package, and that is why it sits at the top. If your property needs trenches for drainage, stumps pulled or a small pond shaped, a backhoe that arrives with the tractor saves you a separate purchase or a rental. Kubota designed the backhoe to attach and detach without tools, so switching back to mowing or snow work takes minutes rather than an afternoon. The spec sheet lists a Kubota diesel, a hydrostatic transmission and four-wheel drive as standard. Owners commonly say it does far more than its size suggests. Its limits are the limits of every sub-compact: it is a light machine, so heavy loader work and large implements are beyond it, and you need the backhoe mounted or a ballast box on the hitch whenever the loader is working. If you will never dig, the package price is hard to justify.
**Pros:** Loader and backhoe in one package; tool-free backhoe removal; 4WD standard; strong resale value. **Cons:** Light frame limits heavy loader work; expensive if you do not need the backhoe.

blocks.h3: Best Dealer Support: John Deere 1025R

blocks.p: The 1025R is built around mowing. Deere's AutoConnect deck lets you drive over the mid-mount mower and clip it on without tools, which matters if the tractor mows every week and does loader or snow work in between. Twin Touch pedals, one for forward and one for reverse, make the hydrostatic drive easy to learn and quick for back-and-forth loader work. Deere's dealer network is the widest in many regions, and the brand offers a long list of matched loaders, backhoes, snow blowers and three-point implements. Owners commonly point to strong resale value. The catch is price: you usually pay more than for a comparable Kioti, LS or Massey Ferguson, and the 1025R is still a light sub-compact, so big implements and heavy ground work belong on a full compact.
**Pros:** Drive-over mower deck; Twin Touch pedals; widest dealer network; large implement catalog. **Cons:** Higher price than similar sub-compacts; light weight limits ground work.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=John+Deere+1025R&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Warranty: Kioti CS2520

blocks.p: Kioti's CS2520 goes head to head with the Deere 1025R and Kubota BX series, usually for less money. Kioti has built its name on warranty terms that often run longer than the big two, though terms change, so ask the dealer for the current coverage in writing. The tractor pairs a diesel engine with a hydrostatic transmission and can be ordered with a front loader and a mid-mount mower deck. Owners commonly describe it as solid for typical small-property jobs: mowing, moving mulch and gravel, light loader work and snow with the right attachment. The real question is the dealer. Kioti's network is growing but is thinner than Deere's or Kubota's in some areas, and resale values are typically lower. With a good Kioti shop nearby, it is the best compact tractor for the money on this list.
**Pros:** Strong price-to-equipment ratio; long warranty terms; diesel and hydrostatic drive. **Cons:** Thinner dealer network in places; lower resale value.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Kioti+CS2520&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best for Larger Acreage: Kubota L2502

blocks.p: The L2502 is a true compact, not a sub-compact, and you feel the difference in weight and capability. It carries a standard Category 1 three-point hitch, so it runs full-size box blades, rotary tillers, post-hole diggers and rotary cutters sized for field work. That makes it the right tractor for five to twenty acres with pasture to brush-hog, a long gravel drive to grade, a big garden to till and firewood to haul. Kubota offers it with either a gear or a hydrostatic transmission, and owners commonly praise its durability. The trade-offs are agility and mowing: it is less nimble around a house and lawn, and many configurations have no mid-mount mower option, so you may still need a separate mower such as one from our [zero turn mower rankings](/best-zero-turn-mower/).
**Pros:** Heavier frame; Category 1 hitch; gear or hydrostatic choice; Kubota reliability. **Cons:** Less nimble on small lawns; no mid-mount deck on many configurations.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Kubota+L2502&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Hydrostatic Feel: Massey Ferguson GC1725M

blocks.p: Owners of the GC1725M most often mention how smooth its hydrostatic transmission feels, which makes it pleasant for both mowing and loader work. It can be fitted with a front loader and a mid-mount mower deck, so it covers the core jobs of a small-property tractor, and the operator station is roomy for the class. Pricing usually lands near Kioti and LS. Massey Ferguson dealers are often full agricultural dealerships, which can be a real plus for parts and service if one is close. The weak spots are a dealer network that varies by region and a smaller range of matched implements than Deere offers. Like every sub-compact, it is best at mowing, light loader work and snow rather than heavy ground engagement.
**Pros:** Smooth hydrostatic drive; comfortable seat; loader and deck options; ag-dealer support. **Cons:** Patchy dealer coverage; fewer matched implements.
[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Massey+Ferguson+GC1725M&tag=sktiger-20)

blocks.h3: Best Budget Pick: LS MT225S

blocks.p: The MT225S is one of the most affordable diesel sub-compacts from an established brand. It brings a hydrostatic transmission, four-wheel drive and options for a front loader and mid-mount mower, which covers what most small-property owners need. LS has offered competitive warranty terms, but confirm the current coverage before you buy. Owners commonly describe it as straightforward and capable for the price. The compromises are the usual ones for a value brand: a smaller dealer network, lower resale value and fewer matched implements. If an LS dealer is close and you would rather spend the budget on a box blade and rotary cutter than on the badge, it is a sensible buy. If the nearest shop is two hours away, the savings may not survive the first breakdown.
**Pros:** Low price for a diesel sub-compact; 4WD and hydrostatic; loader and deck options. **Cons:** Small dealer network; lower resale value.

sections.h: Do You Need a Compact Tractor or Just a Bigger Mower?

blocks.p: You need a tractor only if your land has regular jobs beyond cutting grass. A compact tractor mows, but its real value is the front loader, the three-point hitch and the power take-off (PTO), which let one machine lift, dig, grade, till, haul and clear snow.

blocks.h3: When is a mower the smarter buy?

blocks.p: If mowing is 90 percent of the work, a tractor is usually the wrong purchase. A zero-turn or lawn tractor cuts faster, costs far less and takes up less space. Steep banks near the house are safer with a rear-drive walk-behind, which our [self-propelled mower guide](/best-self-propelled-lawn-mower/) covers.

blocks.h3: Which jobs justify a tractor?

blocks.p: The case builds when your list includes moving gravel, mulch or topsoil, grading a gravel drive, brush-hogging pasture, tilling a large garden, shifting firewood or round bales, digging trenches, or plowing a long driveway. Owners of two acres or more with several of those jobs tend to find a sub-compact earns its keep.

blocks.h3: How do you size a tractor to your land?

blocks.p: List the toughest task your land throws at you in a typical year, rather than the chore you repeat most. That job sets the minimum tractor. Any tractor will cut grass, but hoisting a round bale or pulling a box blade through hard-packed gravel separates the classes fast.

blocks.h3: Should you rent first?

blocks.p: Many rental yards rent compact tractors and mini excavators by the day. If most of your list is a one-time project, like building a driveway or clearing a lot, renting for the project and buying a mower for upkeep can cost far less than owning.

sections.h: What Is the Difference Between a Sub-Compact and a Compact Tractor?

blocks.p: Size, weight and the implements each can carry. Sub-compacts are the smallest class: engines in the low-to-mid 20s of horsepower, operating weights well under 2,000 pounds before attachments, and usually a drive-over mid-mount mower. Compact tractors run from the mid-20s to about 60 horsepower, weigh more, have stouter frames and loaders, and carry a full Category 1 hitch.

blocks.h3: Which class fits your acreage?

blocks.p: Sub-compacts suit two to five acres of mowing, light loader work and snow. Compacts suit five to twenty acres with pasture, firewood and heavier ground work. Many owners say they wish they had bought one size larger, so if you are torn, lean bigger unless storage or close-in mowing rules it out.

blocks.h3: Will it fit where you store it?

blocks.p: Storage settles a lot of these decisions. A sub-compact with the loader removed fits many garage bays; a compact with a loader usually needs a pole barn or a dedicated shed. Measure the door height against the tractor with the rollover bar (ROPS) raised, since that bar is often the highest point.

blocks.h3: What tractor is smaller than a John Deere 1025R?

blocks.p: Below the sub-compact class you are into garden tractors and lawn tractors, which have mid-mount decks but no real loader or Category 1 hitch. If you need a loader at all, a sub-compact like the 1025R or BX23S is the practical floor.

sections.h: Why Does Tractor Weight Matter More Than Horsepower?

blocks.p: Because traction runs out before engine power does on most small-property jobs. Pulling a box blade through packed gravel, pushing a bucket into a dirt pile or yanking a stump all depend on grip, and grip comes from weight on the tires. A light tractor often spins its wheels long before it uses its horsepower, which is why two machines with similar engines can feel completely different in the field.

blocks.h3: How does weight affect stability?

blocks.p: A heavier tractor is steadier when the loader is raised. That is why manufacturers call for rear ballast, such as a weighted box on the hitch or liquid-filled rear tires, any time the loader is working.

blocks.h3: What should you compare on a compact tractor comparison chart?

blocks.p: Put operating weight, loader lift capacity, hitch lift capacity and PTO horsepower side by side, along with wheelbase and overall width if you have tight gates or a narrow barn door. Then hold those numbers up against your heaviest job. Brochure horsepower belongs at the bottom of the chart, not the top.

blocks.h3: How do you add weight?

blocks.p: Loading the rear tires is the popular permanent fix: a tire shop fills them with ballast fluid, adding several hundred pounds low on the machine. Owners who do a lot of loader work often combine loaded tires with a ballast box for the heaviest lifts.

sections.h: Which Three-Point Hitch, PTO and Transmission Do You Need?

blocks.p: Match the hitch category, hitch lift capacity and PTO horsepower to your heaviest implement, and pick a hydrostatic transmission unless you have big fields to work.

blocks.h3: What hitch category do you need?

blocks.p: Most compacts use Category 1. Many sub-compacts use a limited Category 1 that accepts smaller implements. Check the lift capacity at the hitch points too, since it decides how heavy a tiller or box blade the tractor can raise.

blocks.h3: What does the PTO do?

blocks.p: The power take-off sends engine power to rotary cutters, tillers and snow blowers. The rear PTO normally turns at 540 rpm, and sub-compacts add a mid PTO for mid-mount mowers and some front blowers. PTO horsepower is lower than engine horsepower, and implement makers list the PTO figure they need, so check it for every implement on your list.

blocks.h3: Hydrostatic or gear drive?

blocks.p: Hydrostatic drives use foot pedals for forward and reverse. They are easy to learn, ideal for loader work where you change direction constantly, and smooth for mowing, which is why most sub-compacts use them. Gear drives, offered on some compacts like the L2502, deliver power more efficiently on long, steady work such as tilling or brush-hogging large fields, but they ask you to clutch and shift. Some hydrostatic tractors add low, mid and high ranges: low for loader and ground work, high for travel and mowing.

blocks.h3: How do you set up an implement?

blocks.p: Level it. A box blade that sits out of level side to side or front to back grades badly on any tractor. Most owners dial in top-link length and sway chains by trial and error on a short stretch of driveway.

sections.h: What Should You Look for in a Front Loader and Backhoe?

blocks.p: Look for a loader lift capacity that covers what you actually lift, a skid-steer style quick attach, and a third-function valve if you will run a grapple. Add a backhoe only if you dig regularly.

blocks.h3: How is loader lift capacity measured?

blocks.p: Spec sheets usually list capacity at the pivot pin, and sometimes at a point ahead of it. The figure at the bucket edge is lower, so compare both numbers with the loads you plan to move.

blocks.h3: Why does a quick attach matter?

blocks.p: It lets you swap buckets, pallet forks and grapples in moments, and the skid-steer standard opens up a huge aftermarket of attachments.

blocks.h3: Is a third-function valve worth it?

blocks.p: If you plan to move brush, logs or rocks with a grapple, order it with the tractor. Retrofitting one later costs more.

blocks.h3: Is a backhoe worth it on a compact tractor?

blocks.p: A backhoe turns the tractor into a small excavator for trenches, stumps, drainage and footings. Backhoes are expensive and add several thousand dollars to the package, according to typical dealer quotes, so for occasional digging a rented mini excavator is often cheaper. A mounted backhoe also doubles as rear ballast during loader work, which is why many TLB owners leave it on. Check digging depth and reach on the spec sheet against your jobs; a sub-compact backhoe handles drainage trenches well but will not replace a full-size excavator.

blocks.h3: How do you use a loader safely?

blocks.p: Always run rear ballast, carry loads low while traveling and stay off slopes with the bucket raised. Most loader rollovers start with a high bucket on uneven ground.

sections.h: What Implements Do You Need for Snow, Firewood and Grading?

blocks.p: Most owners start with a box blade, a rotary cutter, a rear blade and pallet forks, then add a tiller or snow blower as the seasons demand. The tractor is only part of the spend.

blocks.h3: What does each implement do?

blocks.p: The box blade grades driveways and spreads gravel. The rotary cutter knocks down brush and pasture. The rear blade pushes snow and shapes ditches. The tiller works the garden. Pallet forks move firewood, bales and anything else on a pallet, and they pair well with a [log splitter](/best-log-splitter/) if you heat with wood.

blocks.h3: Is a compact tractor good for snow removal?

blocks.p: Yes. A sub-compact can run a front-mounted blower off the mid PTO, a rear-mounted blower off the rear PTO, a front blade or just the loader bucket. Front blowers let you drive forward and watch the work but need a mid PTO and mounting frame. Rear blowers are cheaper but mean long stretches in reverse. Blades and buckets handle short drives and wet snow but pile it along the edges, which becomes a problem after a few storms. Fit chains or industrial tires, leave the ballast on and use winter diesel or an anti-gel additive.

blocks.h3: Which tires should you choose?

blocks.p: Turf tires spare lawns but slip in mud and snow. Agricultural (R1) tires grip hardest but tear up turf. Industrial (R4) tires sit in between and suit owners who mix loader work with some mowing. Changing tire types later is expensive, so decide at purchase.

blocks.h3: Are used implements a good idea?

blocks.p: Box blades, rear blades and rotary cutters are simple and often turn up used. Check for cracks, worn bearings and bent PTO shafts, and size each implement to the tractor's hitch and PTO rating.

sections.h: How Do You Choose a Dealer, and How Much Does a Compact Tractor Cost?

blocks.p: Choose the dealer as carefully as the tractor, and budget for the tractor, loader and implements as one package.

blocks.h3: What should you ask a dealer?

blocks.p: Ask about service turnaround in peak season, pickup and delivery, parts on the shelf and technician experience. Talk to local owners about how the shop treats them. Deere and Kubota have the widest networks and the strongest resale; Kioti, Massey Ferguson and LS compete on price and warranty with thinner coverage in some areas. An excellent local dealer for a smaller brand can beat a distant dealer for a big one.

blocks.h3: How much does a compact tractor cost?

blocks.p: Dealer quotes commonly put a sub-compact with a loader somewhere around the high teens to about thirty thousand dollars, a TLB package above that, and a full compact with a loader from the mid-twenties into the forties, depending on horsepower, transmission and options. A starter set of box blade, rotary cutter and rear blade adds several thousand more. Compare whole-package prices, including delivery, setup and the first service.

blocks.h3: Is a used compact tractor a good deal?

blocks.p: It can be. Have a mechanic look it over, check the hour meter and service records, and inspect the loader pins, hydraulic hoses and transmission behavior under load.

blocks.h3: How do you keep a tractor running for decades?

blocks.p: Service by the hour meter. Change engine oil and filters, replace the fuel filter, keep the air filter clean, change hydraulic and transmission fluid on schedule and grease the loader, front axle and hitch pivots at the interval in the manual. Drain water from the fuel separator, store the tractor under cover and keep the battery on a maintainer through long idle spells. A simple service log also helps resale.

sections.h: How Do You Operate a Compact Tractor Safely?

blocks.p: Keep the rollover protective structure (ROPS) up and the seat belt fastened. Rollovers are the leading cause of tractor-related deaths, and a folded ROPS protects no one. Lower it only when clearance forces you to, leave the belt off while it is down, drive with extreme care and raise it again as soon as you can.

blocks.h3: How do you avoid a rollover?

blocks.p: Stay away from steep slopes, ditch edges and embankments. Carry loads low, run rear ballast whenever the loader is on and slow down on uneven ground.

blocks.h3: Why is the PTO so dangerous?

blocks.p: A spinning shaft can grab clothing or a limb in an instant. Keep the shields in place, wear close-fitting clothes and never step over a turning shaft. Disengage the PTO, stop the engine and pull the key before touching an implement.

blocks.h3: What other habits matter?

blocks.p: No passengers unless there is an approved seat. Keep children well away from a running tractor. Climb on and off facing the machine using the steps and handles. Every time you leave the seat, lower the loader and implements, set the parking brake and take the key. If you are new to tractors, a short safety course is time well spent.

mistakes: Shopping on horsepower instead of weight

Traction and stability come from weight, and a light tractor spins its tires on many jobs before it runs out of engine. Compare operating weight, loader capacity and hitch lift capacity against your heaviest regular job, and treat the horsepower figure as a tiebreaker rather than the headline.
Picking the brand before the dealer

You will depend on service and parts for years. A strong local dealer with quick turnaround can matter more than the logo, because a two-week repair wait in haying or snow season is expensive. Visit the shops and ask local owners before you commit to any brand.

A loader without rear ballast can lift the back wheels off the ground and tip the tractor forward or sideways. Use a ballast box, the mounted backhoe or loaded rear tires as the manual directs, carry loads low and never travel with the bucket high.
Leaving implements out of the budget

The tractor is only part of the bill. Box blades, rotary cutters, rear blades and forks add thousands more. Plan the implement list alongside the tractor, size each one to the hitch and PTO, and look at used implements to stretch the money.
Driving with the ROPS folded down

The rollover bar only protects you when it is raised and you are belted in. Most tractor deaths involve rollovers. Fold it only for a low doorway or branch, drive very carefully while it is down and put it back up immediately afterward.
bottomLine: Start with the heaviest job your land asks for, then choose the size class, weight and hitch category that can handle it. On most two-to-five-acre properties a sub-compact is enough: the Kubota BX23S if you will dig, the John Deere 1025R if you mow every week and want a close dealer, and the Kioti CS2520 if you want the best compact tractor for the money. Larger properties with pasture and heavier work call for the Kubota L2502. Vet the dealer as hard as the tractor, budget for implements from day one, and keep the ROPS up, the belt on and ballast on the back.

faqs.q: What is the best compact tractor?
faqs.a: The Kubota BX23S is the best compact tractor for most two-to-five-acre properties because it comes as a loader and quick-attach backhoe package with 4WD standard. Choose the John Deere 1025R for mowing and dealer support, the Kioti CS2520 for value, or the full-compact Kubota L2502 for five to twenty acres of heavier ground work.

faqs.q: What is the best compact tractor for the money?
faqs.a: The Kioti CS2520 usually delivers the most tractor per dollar, with a diesel engine, hydrostatic drive, loader and deck options and warranty terms that often run longer than Deere or Kubota. The LS MT225S costs even less. Both depend on having a good dealer nearby, so check service distance before you buy.

faqs.q: What is the best 25 hp compact tractor?
faqs.a: Among tractors in the roughly 25-horsepower class, the Kubota BX23S is the best all-rounder for small properties, and the Kubota L2502 is the best choice when you need a heavier frame and a full Category 1 hitch. Similar horsepower hides big differences in weight and hitch capacity, so compare those numbers first.

faqs.q: What is the best sub compact tractor?
faqs.a: The Kubota BX23S is the best sub-compact tractor if you need a backhoe, and the John Deere 1025R is the best if mowing is a weekly job, thanks to its drive-over AutoConnect deck. The Kioti CS2520 and LS MT225S are the value picks for buyers with a nearby dealer for those brands.

faqs.q: Which compact tractor brands hold resale value best?
faqs.a: John Deere and Kubota generally hold their value best, helped by brand recognition and wide dealer networks. Kioti, Massey Ferguson and LS often cost less up front and resell for less. Hours, condition and service records weigh heavily too, so a well-kept tractor of any brand sells faster than a neglected one.

faqs.q: How many acres do you need for a compact tractor?
faqs.a: Jobs matter more than acreage, but two acres is the usual starting point. Owners with two or more acres who move gravel, grade a drive, brush-hog or plow snow often find a sub-compact worth it. If you only mow, a zero-turn or lawn tractor is cheaper and faster for the same ground.

faqs.q: Does a compact tractor need four-wheel drive?
faqs.a: Yes, for most owners. Driving all four wheels gives you grip for loader jobs, hills, snow and soft soil, and it is the safer setup on a grade. Nearly every sub-compact and compact sold with a loader has 4WD as standard, including every tractor on this list. Two-wheel drive mostly appears on basic flat-ground mowing models.
